verses.text: A prayer for someone who’s suffering, worn down, and pouring out their trouble before the LORD. Hear my prayer, LORD! Let my cry reach you.
Don’t hide your face when trouble hits me. Lean in and listen. When I call, answer quickly.
My days disappear like smoke. My bones burn like a torch.
My heart has dried up like grass in the heat. I even forget to eat.
I groan so much that I’m nothing but skin and bones.
I’m like a pelican out in the wilderness, like an owl in a ruined place.
I lie awake, like a sparrow all alone on the roof.
My enemies insult me all day. Those who rage against me turn my name into a curse.
I eat ashes like bread and mix my drink with tears
because of your fierce anger. You picked me up and threw me aside.
My days are like a shadow stretching long. I’ve dried up like grass.
But you, LORD, will be here forever. Every generation will know your name.
You’ll rise and have mercy on Zion. It’s time to show her compassion. The time you set has come.
Your servants love her stones. Even her dust moves them to pity.
The nations will fear the LORD’s name, and every king on earth will stand in awe of your glory.
The LORD has rebuilt Zion and shown up in his glory.
He answered the prayer of people who had nothing. He didn’t brush off their prayer.
Write this down for the next generation, so a people yet to be created will praise the LORD.
He looked down from his sanctuary high above. From heaven the LORD looked at the earth
to hear prisoners groaning and set free those sentenced to death,
so people would tell of the LORD’s name in Zion and sing his praise in Jerusalem,
when peoples and kingdoms gather together to serve the LORD.
He drained my strength along the way. He cut my days short.
I said, “My God, don’t take me away halfway through my life. Your years stretch across every generation.
Long ago you laid the earth’s foundation. The heavens are your handiwork.
They’ll perish, but you’ll still be here. They’ll all wear out like clothes. You’ll change them like a coat, and they’ll be changed.
But you stay the same. Your years never end.
Your servants’ children will live on, and their descendants will stand secure before you.”
